items.title: U.S. Banks: Third-Quarter Earnings Preview
items.summary: We see the operating environment for year's end as offering a healthy jumping-off point for banks' net interest income growth. We see the best-positioned banks as those with a commercial focus, healthy capital bases and limited credit concerns. We're upgrading FITB to Buy.

items.title: Global Commodities: Optimized Strategy Implementation Outshines
items.summary: Geopolitical volatility has weighed on systematic commodities volatility carry strategies, but optimized implementations have led to significant outperformance. The volatility premium remains rich for oil and products given U.S.-Iran uncertainty. We offer further analysis in this note.

items.title: Midstream Sound Bites: A Refined-Products Export Ban?
items.summary: We consider the midstream implications of a possible refined-products export ban. We see four primary areas where midstream operators could be impacted, with three positives and a potential negative, and offer more analysis in this note. We'd expect such a ban to be relatively short-lived.

items.title: Refining Stocks Pull Back Amid Talk of a Diesel Export Ban
items.summary: In the event of a complete ban on diesel exports, it would take some two months for current distillate inventories to reach historical peak levels, all else equal. But refineries would likely reduce throughput in response to sharply lower margins, with cascading impacts on other prices.

items.title: Are We Near a Peak in Large-Scale Broker Consolidation?
items.summary: We think the endgame for broker M&A isn’t when the tail of the industry is consolidated, but when large assets become scarce, and the industry is down to ~6 large assets that could reasonably be acquired by large, publicly traded brokers. We consider the landscape and possibilities herein.

items.title: Germany Fiscal Monitor: Has Fiscal Package Reached the Economy?
items.summary: Germany’s economy seems on track for better-than-expected growth in 2026. How much does the country's fiscal package have to do with it? We investigate whether there are signs already to be seen that the fiscal expansion is supporting economic activity.

items.title: U.S. Economics Weekly:  Hawkish Fed Will Slow Non-AI Economy
items.summary: The risks of more near-term Fed hikes have increased given recent comments from Chair Warsh. Tighter monetary policy won't noticeably slow AI tailwinds to growth but will have consequences elsewhere, leaving economic growth increasingly dependent on just one driver and so more fragile.

items.title: U.S.-China Summit Preview: High Stakes, Practical Progress
items.summary: We expect practical progress rather than a "grand bargain" from President Xi's U.S. state visit, with an extended trade truce and a formal AI dialogue focused on security guardrails among the possibilities. Geopolitics remains the wildcard to watch, and could spill into the economic track.

items.title: Global Semiconductors: eSSD Demand to Rise Sharply in 2027
items.summary: Continual learning and AI inference are set to drive a sharp increase in eSSD demand, which we forecast to grow 52.9% year over year in 2027.  As memory makers prioritize DRAM/HBM capacity expansion over NAND, NAND supply-demand conditions should tighten materially, resulting in deficits.

items.title: Inflation Weekly: Will Rising Diesel Costs Lift Goods Prices?
items.summary: A renewed increase in energy prices has caused new concerns about pass-through to core inflation, particularly as elevated diesel prices mean higher transportation costs for goods. But recent evidence is limited about the correlation between higher diesel prices and core goods in CPI.

items.title: Malaysia Equity Strategy: Macro Supportive, Themes Intact
items.summary: We remain constructive on Malaysia, supported by a resilient macro backdrop, with 5.1% GDP growth forecast in 2026, contained inflation and a relatively benign domestic rates outlook. The key debate has shifted from domestic fundamentals to global rates, as we explore in this note.

items.title: Argentina's Election and the “Knife-Edge” Narrative
items.summary: We think the "knife-edge" narrative ahead of Argentina's presidential election next fall overstates the real risk, as we see improving macro fundamentals continuing to outweigh rising political noise. We offer our thoughts on strategies for various asset classes in this note.

items.title: U.S. Rates Weekly: Only Hawks Outside the Window
items.summary: Chair Warsh was unquestionably hawkish, but this should limit downside tails for the long end of the curve for now. Core long positions face two challenges: avoiding an October rate hike and weathering seasonally strong January and February core PCE prints. We're concerned on both fronts.

items.title: PULSE Monitor: Resilience or Complacency?
items.summary: The index has held up despite a difficult few weeks of headlines, raising the question of whether the index price action is resilient or complacent. We're more in the resilient camp given drawdowns in consumer and rate sensitive defensives that have taken place under the index surface.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence: Where Intelligence Compounds
items.summary: Early evidence that recursive self-improvement may scale points to a new source of compute demand. Refocusing compute capacity from developing performance to safety, auditability, and alignment is unlikely to impact 2026 and 2027 projections for global capex related to AI demand.

items.title: Global Macro Strategy:  Higher Yields Are the Price of Resilience
items.summary: In a world where the energy intensity of GDP continues to structurally fall, we may need bigger shocks to turn bearish. The Bank of Japan may underwhelm front-end pricing unless they open the door to B2B hikes. We would fade weakness in JPY on this, given structural repatriation risk.

items.title: Emerging Markets Strategy Weekly: Rough Waters Ahead
items.summary: The resumption of Fed hikes has generally been bearish for emerging-markets local currency assets, and we've seen a significant increase in headwinds for EM local asset performance in the last few weeks. We explore the factors at work in this note.

items.title: European Rates Weekly: A QT Revolution
items.summary: The Bank of England made sweeping changes to QT, although the market impact is likely short-lived. We offer further suggested strategies in this note.

items.title: We're Downgrading Boston Scientific to Neutral
items.summary: We've lowered estimates for Boston Scientific eight times this year and aren't certain we've reached the final revision or what the path to recovery is. While we're saddened by this turn of events, we're stepping aside, downgrading BSX to Neutral, and lowering our target price to $50.

items.title: Global FX Strategy: USD Squeeze Could Have Legs for Now
items.summary: A hawkish Fed, geopolitical risks and general risk-off make for about as bullish a USD backdrop as we can get. The more hawkish reaction function could keep yields and the USD elevated until we have more clarity on U.S.-Iran de-escalation, which remains unlikely before the midterms.

items.title: Our Takeaways From the State of the European Union
items.summary: In her State of the European Union address, President von der Leyen reiterated the direction of increased energy independence, higher defense spending, accelerated AI adoption, and increased supply chain/critical mineral resilience. We analyze key announcements and investment implications.

items.title: U.S. Semiconductors: AI Infra Summit Day 2 Takeaways
items.summary: For Day 2 of the AI Infra Summit we focus on networking-specific takeaways. As AI workloads become more reasoning-intensive and context-rich, infrastructure scaling will also depend on innovations across memory hierarchies, HBM, system architectures, and networking fabrics.

items.title: India Economics: Enhancing Savings and Investments
items.summary: We offer a scenario analysis to project India's savings and investments requirements over the next decade and identify the financing gap. We explore some policy issues concerning household savings, at an aggregate level as well as regarding allocation toward different asset classes.

items.title: Australia Banks: A Stronger Investment Cycle
items.summary: We expect a multi-year period of elevated business investment in Australia's "two-speed economy," which should support business credit growth. The growing split between business and housing growth highlights the relative valuation attractiveness of NAB, which we're upgrading to Buy.

items.title: Fed Raises Rates 25 Basis Points, With a Hawkish Tone
items.summary: Details of the FOMC meeting, including a unanimous 25-basis-point rate hike and a median “dot” showing one more such hike this year, were close to our and market expectations. We offer further analysis in this note.  In our base case, the Fed resumes rate cuts in June.

items.title: Global Equity Strategy: The Fed and the Long End
items.summary: Risks from more restrictive monetary policy have compounded worries about higher long-end bond yields. So will higher yields derail the bull market in equities? We analyze the historical record and explore why it suggests more short-term caution amid stagflationary risks from geopolitics.

items.title: Oil Monitor: Uncertain Times
items.summary: Saudi Arabia's shutdown of the East-West pipeline highlighted that regional energy infrastructure remains vulnerable and risks are no longer confined to the Strait of Hormuz. Recent strong price action has also been supported by physical-market strength beyond geopolitical headlines.

items.title: U.S. Semiconductors: AI Infra Summit Day 1 Takeaways
items.summary: Our takeaways from Day 1 of the AI Infra Summit include that fundamentally, frontier AI model developers see AI safety and alignment as a compute-intensive process. This implies that — contrary to investor worries — safety concerns may drive more, rather than less, demand for compute.

items.title: Emerging Markets El Niño Monthly Tracker
items.summary: We look at emerging-markets rainfall forecasts for the rest of the year. EM food inflation momentum rose toward its recent averages, with more pronounced pick-ups in EM Asia, Nigeria and Chile but a very benign picture in Mexico, central and eastern Europe, and Israel.

items.title: Brazil Elections and the Need for Fiscal Reforms
items.summary: With the presidential election near, we look at Brazil's need for fiscal reforms, as some sort of adjustment in the next administration seems unavoidable. In this third report, we explain why we believe Brazil may benefit from a HR reform that changes the labor regime of public servants.
